hints.title: Triangle Inequality on Sorted Sides
hints.text: Three side lengths a <= b <= c form a valid non-degenerate triangle if and only if a + b > c.

hints.title: Descending Triplet Scanning
hints.text: Sort the array descending. The first adjacent triplet satisfying nums[i + 1] + nums[i + 2] > nums[i] yields the largest possible perimeter.

hints.title: Greedy Single-Pass Evaluation
hints.text: Sort nums in reverse. For index i from 0 to len(nums) - 3: if nums[i + 1] + nums[i + 2] > nums[i], return nums[i] + nums[i + 1] + nums[i + 2]. If loop finishes with no valid triplet, return 0.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all O(N^3) triplets causes timeout for N up to 10000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting enables an immediate linear sweep checking consecutive triplets, requiring O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should prove why checking adjacent sorted elements guarantees finding the maximum perimeter.
complexity.notes: If nums[i + 1] + nums[i + 2] <= nums[i], any smaller pair with nums[i] will also fail.
